On 30 August 2006 at 5.15 p.m., the applicants were approached by a group of police officers who asked whether they had authorisation for the demonstration.
After the attack by the person in Special Forces uniform, the other demonstration participants were immediately surrounded by a group of police officers and taken to a police van.

Section 6(1) of the Moldovan Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be conducted peacefully, without any sort of weapons, and shall ensure the protection of participants and the environment, without impeding the normal use of public highways, road traffic and the operation of economic undertakings and without degenerating into acts of violence capable of endangering the public order and the physical integrity and life of persons or their property.

Section 7 of the Moldovan Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be suspended in circumstances including: denial and defamation of the State and of the people; incitement to war or aggression and incitement to hatred on ethnic, racial or religious grounds; incitement to discrimination, territorial separatism or public violence; and acts that undermine the constitutional order.

Section 11(1) of the Moldovan Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that not later than fifteen days prior to the date of the assembly, the organiser shall submit a notification to the Municipal Council.

Article 174 § 1(2) of the Moldovan Code of Administrative Offences, in force at the material time, provides that the organisation and holding of an assembly without prior notification to the Municipal Council or without authorisation from the Council, or in breach of the conditions concerning the conduct of meetings indicated in the authorisation, shall be punishable by a fine imposed on the organisers (leaders) of the assembly in an amount equal to between MDL 500 and 1,000.

Article 174 § 1(4) of the Moldovan Code of Administrative Offences, in force at the material time, provides that active participation in an assembly referred to in paragraph 2 of Article 174 § 1 shall be punishable by a fine in an amount between MDL 200 and 300.

On 29 August 2006, the Chişinău Court of Appeal found that the Chişinău Municipality's refusal to authorise the demonstration for the full requested period had been unlawful.
On 29 August 2006, the Chişinău Court of Appeal quashed the Chişinău Municipal Council's decision of 18 July 2006.
On 1 November 2006, the Supreme Court of Justice quashed the judgment of the Chişinău Court of Appeal of 29 August 2006.
On 1 November 2006, the Supreme Court of Justice dismissed the applicants' action, finding that the Chişinău Municipal Council's decision of 18 July 2006 was lawful.
